parsed_output.analysis: The specification defines a very small set of required behaviours: power-on to Human Driving Mode, front_distance > 10 to Autonomous Mode, a return to Human Driving Mode on human steering cmd + brake pressed but only while in the auto final sub-state, and a power-off move to a final state. The PlantUML model implements a HumanDrivingMode simple state and an AutonomousMode composite with three sub-states, and it does implement the front_distance > 10 entry to AutonomousMode. Deviations are in the power-on entry, the allowed return conditions from the autonomous sub-machine, and the power-off target.

issues.issue: Power-on entry is not labelled / guarded
issues.reason: Specification 3 requires 'when power on, the system turn into human driving mode'. The model shows an unlabeled initial transition [*] -> HumanDrivingMode with no Power On trigger/guard, so the required power-on condition is not represented.

issues.issue: Return to Human Driving Mode is allowed from AutoOperationalState
issues.reason: Specification 4 states transit to human driving mode on human steering cmd, brake pressed 'in (auto final)'. The model also provides the same transition from AutoOperationalState, i.e., from a non-final autonomous sub-state, which is not permitted by the specification.
issues.where: AutoOperationalState -> HumanDrivingMode : human steering cmd, brake pressed

issues.issue: Power-off transitions to termination [*] instead of a final state
issues.reason: Specification 5 requires 'when power off, it will transit to final state'. The model terminates the machine with the pseudostate [*] on Power Off from both HumanDrivingMode and AutonomousMode. No named final state is reached; the behaviour is termination rather than a transition to a specified final state.
issues.where: HumanDrivingMode -> [*] : Power Off and AutonomousMode -> [*] : Power Off

system_prompt:
You are an experienced control-systems engineer reviewing a state machine model against the natural-language specification it was built from.

You are given two things, both complete and unmodified:
  1. The natural-language specification.
  2. A state machine model written in PlantUML.

Your task: identify the places where the model does not conform to the specification. Read the specification in full first, then read the model in full, then report what you find.

Report as many or as few issues as you actually find, and organize them however you judge best. For each issue, state what the non-conformance is, which part of the model it concerns, and why you consider it a non-conformance.

Write your findings in en-US. Return only the requested structured response.
user_prompt:
## Natural-language specification

1 The human driving mode is represented by a simple state. 2 The autonomous mode has sub-states and is represented by a sub machine state. 3. when power on, the system turn into human driving mode 4when front_distance > 10, auto transport to autonomous state 4. transit to human driving mode when receive human steering cmd, brake pressed, in (auto final) 5 when power off, it will transit to final state

## State machine model (PlantUML)

@startuml
[*] -> HumanDrivingMode
HumanDrivingMode: Human Driving Mode
HumanDrivingMode -> AutonomousMode: front_distance > 10
AutonomousMode: Autonomous Mode
state AutonomousMode {
[*] -> AutoInitialState
AutoInitialState: Initial State
AutoInitialState -> AutoOperationalState: Signal Transmission Succeeds
AutoOperationalState: Operational State
AutoOperationalState -> AutoFinalState: Mission Completed
AutoFinalState: Final State
AutoOperationalState -> HumanDrivingMode: human steering cmd, brake pressed
AutoFinalState -> HumanDrivingMode: human steering cmd, brake pressed
}
HumanDrivingMode -> [*]: Power Off
AutonomousMode -> [*]: Power Off
@enduml
